incident-bot: [P1 ALERT] GPU pool us-west-2-a/gpu-xlarge: queue growth > 90% for 10m, throttled requests increasing, autoscaler unable to provision due to binpacking failures. Ticket created: INC-4447
Aisha: acked. jumping on it. paging oncall.
oncall-rotation: @Aisha i'm oncall, joining. what's the initial customer impact?
Aisha: 429s and queued requests for hosted API endpoints for some heavy gen customers. Observed median latency spike 3x. Queue backlog ~12k requests across pool.
Priya: grabbing logs from allocator and scheduler. suspect MIG fragmentation — we have many leftover 1/2-GPU slices that aren't packable into new pods.
Luca: can you paste the autoscaler events?
Priya: paste: ```
E0315 14:04:02 autoscaler.go:222] ScaleUpForbidden: no suitable node to schedule pod: insufficient contiguous MIG capacity
E0315 14:05:10 allocator.go:453] binpack: failed to placement on node n-ukr1: free slices 1x1g, 2x1g but requested contiguous 4g
```
Samir: that matches. Recent canary used smaller MIG profiles (1g slices) and now we have mix of 1g and 4g workloads. Autoscaler respects affinity so can't merge slices.
Aisha: customers impacted: 3 mid-market customers hitting sustained bursts — CS-Eli pls notify and provide ETA.
CS-Eli: notified customers on high-impact affected routes. told them we're investigating and will update in 15m.
oncall-rotation: immediate mitigations: (1) increase autoscaler max to allow burst to other pools (2) emergency repack to consolidate slices (3) temporarily relax binpack constraints to allow heterogeneous placement. Thoughts?
Luca: (2) repack is safest long term but takes time and will move other workloads. (3) relaxing constraints may cause perf regressions but can reduce queue quickly.
Priya: starting a dry-run repack simulation now. Command: ```./infra-tool repack --pool us-west-2-a --strategy consolidate --simulate```
Priya: simulation shows ~60% reduction in stranded slices if we convert half of 1g pools to 4g by merging. Estimated time 9-12m for rolling operations.
Aisha: do repack with canary threshold 10% first. run with low-disruption mode. Priya proceed.
Priya: running: ```./infra-tool repack --pool us-west-2-a --strategy consolidate --canary 10% --mode low-disruption```
incident-bot: incident updated: status=investigating, severity=P1, assigned=Aisha+Priya+Luca.
Samir: while repack runs, increase autoscaler max for us-west-2-a from 200 -> 280 to allow burst into ephemeral capacity. I'll adjust route policies to prefer less-fragmented pools first.
Luca: adjusted autoscaler max. also enabling fallback routing to secondary pool us-west-2-b/gpu-large for non-SLA customers. config snippet: ```route.policy=fallback:us-west-2-b if latency>800ms```
Aisha: monitoring queue; still growing but rate slowed.
Priya: canary repack completed for 10% nodes, no regressions. proceeding to stage 2. progress log: ```repack: stage2 40/120 nodes drained, migrating KV caches with prefix cache-key-.*```
CS-Eli: customers asked for ETA — sharing 30-45m for full mitigation.
Samir: quick fix also done: temporarily loosened scheduler contiguous-MIG requirement for best-effort workloads (`--allow-mixed-mig=true`), that freed up ~800 requests backlog immediately.
Aisha: note: that flag may increase GPU contention, watch token-level latency. Set alert if tail latency > 2s.
incident-bot: [METRIC] queue_length_us-west-2-a decreased from 12k -> 3.2k in 18m. throttled_rate down 78%.
Luca: repack is at 75% now. progress looks good. Some nodes failed to drain due to long-lived sessions (inference sessions with KV cache pinned). Working with app teams to gracefully evict.
Priya: issuing graceful drains with extended timeout 6m for those nodes. logs: ```node n-az45 evict: session drain timeout 2m -> extend 6m```
Aisha: oncall handoff in 30m — @Luca please prepare the post-incident summary and triage items.
Samir: completed scale and repack. all new containers scheduled. queued requests are draining.
incident-bot: incident severity -> mitigated (customers experiencing degraded but stable service).
CS-Eli: customers confirmed fewer failures; one reported residual 500s on legacy route still under investigation.
Aisha: root cause summary for now: mixed MIG sizing + recent canary of smaller slice types led to fragmentation and inability for autoscaler to pack new pods. Autoscaler hit MaxScale while fragmented free slices couldn't be combined. Repack + relax constraints + scale increase mitigated immediate impact.
Luca: next steps: 1) revert allow-mixed-mig flag in 12h if no regressions, 2) schedule automated night repack every 24h with safe thresholds, 3) add preflight check to canary pipeline to warn when new MIG profiles increase fragmentation risk, 4) tune autoscaler to consider slice defragmentation signals.
Priya: opened follow-ups: INFRA-888 (auto-repack job), SCHED-442 (scheduler heuristic), DEPLOY-129 (canary MIG preflight).
Aisha: final note: we're leaving the increased autoscaler cap until the repack job hardens. handoff to day oncall @Luca in 30m.
Luca: taking over. ping me if anything flares.
incident-bot: thread closed for active paging; incident record updated with timeline and mitigations.
Aisha: thanks team — good mitigations.
CS-Eli: customers updated with post-mortem ETA 48h.
Samir: quick metric snapshot to include in postmortem: ```
before: q=12k, 95p latency=2.1s, throttled=4.2k/min
during: q peak=14.1k, throttled peak=6.8k/min
after: q=120, 95p latency=0.42s, throttled=80/min
```
Priya: saving logs for RCA: `/var/logs/alloc/us-west-2-a/4447001234/*.gz`
Luca: will prepare RCA draft. assigning owners. closing oncall.
Aisha: resolved for now. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
